title: No explicit ban on advertising based on inferred disability signals of children

uae_says.statement: SOURCE TO BE VERIFIED: no UAE provision that specifically bans profiling-based or inference-based advertising to children has been confirmed in the knowledge base yet.

global_example_says.statement: Candidate global examples (to be verified): the EU Digital Services Act restricts profiling-based advertising to minors on online platforms, and the EU AI Act prohibits AI practices that exploit vulnerabilities linked to age or disability.

gap_analysis: ANALYSIS (not law): if confirmed, the UAE framework relies on general data-protection and consumer rules, which leaves the inferred-signal case to interpretation.
recommendation: Add an explicit prohibition on using inferred health, disability or learning-difficulty signals of children for advertising.

title: No published risk-classification standard for AI used in education

uae_says.statement: SOURCE TO BE VERIFIED: national AI strategy and ethics documents set principles, but no binding risk tiers for educational AI were found in the knowledge base.

global_example_says.statement: Candidate global example (to be verified): the EU AI Act lists AI used to evaluate students among high-risk uses with conformity requirements.

gap_analysis: ANALYSIS (not law): without risk tiers, accuracy, bias testing and documentation duties for screening models are left to procurement contracts.
recommendation: Publish an education-AI standard: accuracy and bias testing across Arabic and English handwriting, false-positive limits, and documentation duties.

title: Unclear lead authority when consumer, data and education mandates overlap

uae_says.statement: SOURCE TO BE VERIFIED: consumer protection, data protection and education regulators each cover part of the in-app purchase case; no lead-agency rule was found in the knowledge base.

global_example_says.statement: Candidate global example (to be verified): the UK Age Appropriate Design Code is enforced by a single regulator for children's online services.

citations.law: UK ICO Age Appropriate Design Code

gap_analysis: ANALYSIS (not law): overlapping mandates slow the response; the scenario room shows the education and consumer agents disagreeing on suspension versus controls.
recommendation: Agree a lead-agency protocol for edtech cases involving children.

title: No coordination rule for sharing screening results between schools, providers and parents

uae_says.statement: SOURCE TO BE VERIFIED: no rule found on who may see an unreviewed screening flag and when.

global_example_says.statement: Candidate global example (to be verified): the US COPPA framework allows schools to give consent for educational use only, limiting commercial reuse.

citations.law: US Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA)

gap_analysis: ANALYSIS (not law): the false-positive scenario shows a flag reaching a teacher before counsellor review.
recommendation: Define a sharing protocol: flags visible only after counsellor review, with access logs.

title: Early screening benefits versus data minimisation for children

uae_says.statement: SOURCE TO BE VERIFIED: inclusion goals encourage early identification, while data-protection rules call for minimisation; no guidance reconciling them was found.

global_example_says.statement: Candidate global example (to be verified): the EU GDPR sets specific conditions for children's consent and for automated decision-making.

gap_analysis: ANALYSIS (not law): both objectives are legitimate; without guidance, providers may collect more handwriting data than screening needs.
recommendation: Issue guidance on minimum data for screening, on-device processing and retention limits.

title: No edtech-specific rule on processing children's data abroad

uae_says.statement: SOURCE TO BE VERIFIED: general cross-border transfer rules were not yet confirmed in the knowledge base for children's educational data.

global_example_says.statement: Candidate global example (to be verified): the EU GDPR restricts transfers to countries without adequate protection.

gap_analysis: ANALYSIS (not law): the controversy scenario shows a provider moving analytics abroad without notice.
recommendation: Require notice to schools and parents and documented safeguards before any transfer.
